statement:
% Book-local P06.2 polyannulus slope exact sequence, 20 September 2026.
Retain the setting and notation of
\Cref{prop:p062-polyannulus-bundle-slope-local-system,%
def:p062-zero-current-radiance-class}.  Thus
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathscr P_W(U)
 &=\{b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R):\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0\},\\
 \rho_0(\pi)
 &=[(c_{\alpha\beta})]
   \in\check H^1\bigl(W,\mathscr P_W(\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R})\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
We again record the transition data used below.  In the frame indexed by
$\alpha$,
\begin{align*}
 L_\beta
 &=\pi^*c_{\alpha\beta}
   +(M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)L_\alpha,\\
 c_{\alpha\gamma}
 &=c_{\beta\gamma}+M_{\beta\gamma}c_{\alpha\beta},
 &
 a_\alpha&=M_{\alpha\beta}^{\mathsf T}a_\beta.
\end{align*}
Every continuous zero-current function has unique chartwise coefficients
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-slope-exact-local-form}
 h=\pi^*b_\alpha+(a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}L_\alpha,
 \qquad
 b_\alpha=b_\beta+a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta},
\end{equation}
where $b_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)$ and $a_\alpha$ is locally
constant.  Conversely, after refinement, coefficients with these
properties define a continuous zero-current function by
\eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-local-form}.  This local converse is the one for
the displayed curve--polyannulus product charts; it is not asserted for an
arbitrary annular fibration.

After passage to a common refinement, a second set of annular coordinates
is related to the first by
\[
 \widehat L_\alpha
 =\pi^*e_\alpha+(N_\alpha\circ\pi)L_\alpha,
 \qquad
 N_\alpha\in\operatorname{GL}_s(\mathbf Z),
 \qquad
 e_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)^s,
\]
with $N_\alpha$ locally constant.  Its transition data satisfy
\[
 \widehat M_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta M_{\alpha\beta}N_\alpha^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat c_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta c_{\alpha\beta}
  +e_\beta-\widehat M_{\alpha\beta}e_\alpha.
\]

We also record the vanishing criterion for the radiance class.  If
$\rho_0(\pi)=0$, then, after refinement, there are
$d_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)^s$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-slope-exact-radiance-gauge}
 c_{\alpha\beta}+d_\beta-M_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha=0.
\end{equation}
The vectors
\[
 \widetilde L_\alpha=L_\alpha+\pi^*d_\alpha
\]
then satisfy
$\widetilde L_\beta=(M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)\widetilde L_\alpha$ and
glue to a continuous section $\Lambda_\pi$ of the associated flat real
vector bundle on $Y$.  For every parallel dual section $a$, the local
pairings
$(a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde L_\alpha$ glue to a continuous
zero-current function on $Y$ with slope $a$; this is the
preceding local converse with base coefficient
$a_\alpha^{\mathsf T}d_\alpha$.

Put
\[
 \mathscr Z(Y)=
 \{h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R):\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0\}.
\]

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-polyannulus-slope-exact-sequence}
The unique local slope vectors define a linear map
\[
 \sigma_\pi:\mathscr Z(Y)
 \longrightarrow H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee}).
\]
For a parallel dual section $a$, with local coordinates $a_\alpha$, the
scalar functions
\[
 r_{\alpha\beta}(a)=a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta}
 \in\mathscr P_W(U_{\alpha\beta})
\]
form a Cech one-cocycle.  Its class depends only on $a$ and the canonical
radiance class, and defines a linear contraction map
\[
 \partial_{\rho_0}:H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee})
 \longrightarrow\check H^1(W,\mathscr P_W),
 \qquad
 a\longmapsto\langle a,\rho_0(\pi)\rangle.
\]
There is a natural exact sequence of real vector spaces
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-polyannulus-slope-exact-sequence}
 0\longrightarrow\mathscr P_W(W)
 \xrightarrow{\ \pi^*\ }\mathscr Z(Y)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sigma_\pi\ }
 H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee})
 \xrightarrow{\ \partial_{\rho_0}\ }
 \check H^1(W,\mathscr P_W).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, a parallel slope $a$ occurs in a global continuous
zero-current function if and only if
$\langle a,\rho_0(\pi)\rangle=0$.

If $\partial_{\rho_0}$ is injective, every continuous zero-current function
on $Y$ is the pullback of a unique element of $\mathscr P_W(W)$.  In
particular, this holds when
$H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee})=0$.

If $\rho_0(\pi)=0$, any zero-current affine gauge satisfying
\eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-radiance-gauge} gives a splitting of
\eqref{eq:p062-polyannulus-slope-exact-sequence} and hence a
gauge-dependent isomorphism
\[
 \mathscr Z(Y)\simeq
 \mathscr P_W(W)\oplus
 H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee}).
\]
None of these assertions trivializes the integral local system or produces
global analytic annular coordinates.
\end{proposition}
proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $a\in H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee})$.  On a triple overlap,
the affine cocycle and dual transition laws give
\begin{align*}
 r_{\alpha\gamma}(a)
 &=a_\gamma^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\gamma}\\
 &=a_\gamma^{\mathsf T}c_{\beta\gamma}
   +a_\gamma^{\mathsf T}M_{\beta\gamma}c_{\alpha\beta}\\
 &=r_{\beta\gamma}(a)+r_{\alpha\beta}(a),
\end{align*}
because
$a_\beta=M_{\beta\gamma}^{\mathsf T}a_\gamma$.  Thus
$(r_{\alpha\beta}(a))$ is a scalar Cech one-cocycle.

We check that its class is intrinsic.  On a common refinement, suppose a
second set of annular coordinates is related to the first by
\[
 \widehat L_\alpha
 =\pi^*e_\alpha+(N_\alpha\circ\pi)L_\alpha.
\]
The change-of-frame identities from the radiance construction are
\[
 \widehat M_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta M_{\alpha\beta}N_\alpha^{-1},
 \qquad
 \widehat c_{\alpha\beta}
 =N_\beta c_{\alpha\beta}
  +e_\beta-\widehat M_{\alpha\beta}e_\alpha.
\]
The dual coordinates are
$\widehat a_\alpha=N_\alpha^{-\mathsf T}a_\alpha$.  Hence
\[
 \widehat a_\beta^{\mathsf T}\widehat c_{\alpha\beta}
 =a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta}
  +\widehat a_\beta^{\mathsf T}e_\beta
  -\widehat a_\alpha^{\mathsf T}e_\alpha.
\]
The two scalar cocycles differ by a Cech coboundary.  Refinement does not
change their direct-limit class, so $\partial_{\rho_0}$ is well defined and
is the contraction of $a$ with the canonical class $\rho_0(\pi)$.
Linearity is immediate.

The coefficient uniqueness in \eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-local-form} makes
$\sigma_\pi$ well defined and linear.  The map $\pi^*$ in
\eqref{eq:p062-polyannulus-slope-exact-sequence} is injective because the
locally trivial map $\pi$ is surjective.  A pullback has zero local slope.
Conversely, if $\sigma_\pi(h)=0$, then
\eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-local-form} gives $h=\pi^*b_\alpha$, and the
coefficient transition reduces to $b_\alpha=b_\beta$.  The $b_\alpha$
therefore glue to a unique $b\in\mathscr P_W(W)$.  This proves exactness at
$\mathscr P_W(W)$ and $\mathscr Z(Y)$.

For $h\in\mathscr Z(Y)$ with slope $a=\sigma_\pi(h)$, the second identity
in \eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-local-form} reads
\[
 r_{\alpha\beta}(a)=b_\alpha-b_\beta.
\]
Thus $\partial_{\rho_0}(a)=0$, and
$\operatorname{im}\sigma_\pi\subseteq\ker\partial_{\rho_0}$.

Conversely, suppose
$a\in\ker\partial_{\rho_0}$.  By the direct-limit definition of Cech
cohomology, after refining the atlas there are
$b_\alpha\in\mathscr P_W(U_\alpha)$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-slope-obstruction-coboundary}
 b_\alpha-b_\beta=a_\beta^{\mathsf T}c_{\alpha\beta}.
\end{equation}
Define on $\pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)$
\[
 h_\alpha=\pi^*b_\alpha
 +(a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}L_\alpha.
\]
On an overlap, the logarithmic transition law, the dual transition law,
and \eqref{eq:p062-slope-obstruction-coboundary} give
\begin{align*}
 h_\beta
 &=\pi^*b_\beta
   +(a_\beta\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}
     \bigl(\pi^*c_{\alpha\beta}
            +(M_{\alpha\beta}\circ\pi)L_\alpha\bigr)\\
 &=\pi^*b_\alpha
   +(a_\alpha\circ\pi)^{\mathsf T}L_\alpha
 =h_\alpha.
\end{align*}
They therefore glue to a continuous function $h$ on $Y$.  The standing
local converse makes $h$ a zero-current function, and its unique slope is
$a$.  Hence
$\ker\partial_{\rho_0}\subseteq\operatorname{im}\sigma_\pi$, proving
exactness at the parallel-slope term.

If $\partial_{\rho_0}$ is injective, exactness makes
$\sigma_\pi$ identically zero, so the already proved exactness at
$\mathscr Z(Y)$ gives the asserted descent.  The vanishing of the space of
parallel dual sections is a sufficient special case.

Finally, if $\rho_0(\pi)=0$, then $\partial_{\rho_0}=0$, so exactness makes
$\sigma_\pi$ surjective.  Choose the vectors $d_\alpha$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:p062-slope-exact-radiance-gauge}, and let $\Lambda_\pi$ be the
global continuous logarithmic-radius section obtained from the
$\widetilde L_\alpha=L_\alpha+\pi^*d_\alpha$.  The standing local converse
shows that the map
\[
 H^0(W,\mathbb V_{\pi,\mathbf R}^{\vee})\longrightarrow\mathscr Z(Y),
 \qquad
 a\longmapsto\langle\pi^{-1}a,\Lambda_\pi\rangle,
\]
takes values in $\mathscr Z(Y)$; its local formula has slope $a$, so it is
a linear right inverse to $\sigma_\pi$.
Together with the kernel computation, it gives the displayed direct-sum
decomposition.  Its dependence on the affine gauge and the final scope
qualification are exactly those of the radiance construction.
\end{proof}
